$comment: Maps the Content Contract audience vocabulary (ai/openwebui/knowledge/company-wiki/tools/wiki-schema.json)
onto the Open WebUI groups that actually exist on the live instance.
This is the artifact llm-knowledge-base-plan.md Phase 0 calls 'Define the audience and
sensitivity vocabulary and its exact Open WebUI group mapping'. Until it is populated and
signed off by the content owner, upload_kb.py REFUSES to publish any collection that would
need a mapping it does not have — the plan's rule is that a document cannot be published
when its metadata has no valid group mapping, so failing closed is the compliant behavior.
The vocabulary is tier-shaped (erisa-member / erisa-team-lead / erisa-manager) while the live
groups are function-shaped (Erisa - Creator / Erisa - Campaign). That mismatch is exactly why
this file has to be an explicit, reviewed decision rather than something a script infers.
'audiences' maps each vocabulary group to a list of live Open WebUI group NAMES. Names are
resolved to ids at run time against GET /api/v1/groups/, so an added or renamed group fails
loudly instead of silently granting nothing.
'automatic' grants are applied to every collection regardless of sensitivity, per the note in
wiki-schema.json. Keep this list minimal: every entry widens access to all synced content.
